intro: Paired observations share a baseline. Work with within-pair differences before comparing their average change with its sampling variability.
task: Return the mean paired difference, its estimated standard error, and the corresponding t statistic without computing a p-value.
requirements: before and after are equal-length vectors containing at least two pairs. The difference direction is after-before.
Use sample variance with denominator n-1, then standard_error=sample_std/sqrt(n) and t=mean_difference/standard_error.
Reject difference standard deviation at or below 1e-12. Return {"mean_difference": mean, "standard_error": se, "t": statistic, "degrees_of_freedom": n-1}.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Calculate after-minus-before within each pair before estimating any mean or variance.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Use the sample standard deviation of differences, then divide by the square root of the number of pairs.

explanation: Pairing removes the shared baseline before estimating variability. The spread that matters is the spread of differences, not the separate spreads of the two measurement vectors.

The statistic divides average change by its estimated standard error. Converting it into an inferential conclusion requires assumptions and a reference distribution beyond this computational exercise.
